items.reason: Pinning by digest means asking GitHub what each tag points at right now and this session has no network; `npm run actions:pin` already does the whole close (resolve, rewrite, flip STRICT=true and RATCHET.pinned) in one networked run, and the broad-write half is already narrow and justified in .github/workflow-permissions.json.

The `<name>` / `<name>:check` / `<name>:drill` shape is this repository's uniform convention across ~40 gate scripts rather than three one-off aliases, and the specific names are pinned by blocking tests (test-unit/typecheck-strict.test.mjs, test-unit/gate-timings.test.mjs, test-unit/api-surface.test.mjs) plus .github/constraint-map.json, so collapsing three families would break the suite and make the surface less predictable, not more; the same class of duplication one layer down — five hand-copied `check:ci` chain parsers — was collapsed into scripts/lib/chain.mjs instead.

The trailer is produced by .husky/prepare-commit-msg (installed by `npm install` via scripts/install-commit-hooks.mjs) and the bypass is structural — a lane that commits in a throwaway worktree where nobody ran `npm install` runs no hooks at all, which is exactly how this Ascent lane commits — so closing it needs the commit-producing harness to set AGENT_HARNESS/COMMIT_ATTRIBUTION or write the trailers itself (scripts/issue-dispatch.mjs is the in-repo worked example); confirming which paths actually bypass needs git history this session cannot read, and ADR-0007 forbids promoting the coverage report to a gate at 53%.

`check:ci` now runs `test:unit` before `npm run check`, so the suite's verdict arrives before `next build` instead of after it, and scripts/gate-timings.mjs's cheapest-first rule was generalised from the seconds boundary to full bucket monotonicity so this class of ordering defect can go red at all.

lessons: This repository's own blocking tests pin the shape of its tooling — script names, chain order, remedy table, constraint map — so a 'simple' package.json or gate-chain edit ripples into ~6 test files; read test-unit/gate-remedy.test.mjs, gate-timings.test.mjs, constraint-map.test.mjs and delivery-contract.test.mjs BEFORE touching package.json scripts.

A gate whose rule stops one notch short of where the cost is reads as fully enforced: cheapest-first was checked only across the seconds boundary, so the 517-file unit suite sat behind `next build` for months with every check green. When auditing an ordering or ratchet rule here, ask which adjacent step the rule cannot see.
Ceilings in .github/guidance-budget.json are EXACT line counts of the read-first documents, so any edit to AGENTS.md must be line-neutral or arrive with the ceiling raised in the same diff.

An offline session cannot close D9 action-pinning here, and the repository already knows it: scripts/actions-pin.mjs --update resolves, rewrites, and flips its own STRICT/RATCHET in one pass. The honest dispatch for that row is a human running one command, not another agent cycle.
